claim: Salicylate specifically inhibits CBP and p300 lysine acetyltransferase activity in vitro by direct competition with acetyl-Coenzyme A at the catalytic site.
source: Here we show that salicylate specifically inhibits CBP and p300 lysine acetyltransferase activity in vitro by direct competition with acetyl-Coenzyme A at the catalytic site.
evidence: Supported by in vitro HAT assays showing dose-dependent inhibition (Figure 1A), thermal stability assays showing salicylate binding to p300 (Figure 1B), and Lineweaver-Burk kinetic analysis demonstrating competitive inhibition with acetyl-CoA (Figure 1C)

claim: Diflunisal inhibits p300 more potently than salicylate.
source: We used a chemical structure-similarity search to identify another anti-inflammatory drug, diflunisal, that inhibits p300 more potently than salicylate.
evidence: Supported by in vitro HAT assays showing IC50 values: diflunisal IC50 = 1.05 mM vs salicylate IC50 = 6.12 mM (Figure 3A, B)

claim: At concentrations attainable in human plasma after oral administration, both salicylate and diflunisal blocked the acetylation of lysine residues on histone and non-histone proteins in cells.
source: At concentrations attainable in human plasma after oral administration, both salicylate and diflunisal blocked the acetylation of lysine residues on histone and non-histone proteins in cells.
evidence: Supported by Western blot data showing deacetylation of histones (Figure 2A, 3C) and non-histone proteins NF-κB and p53 (Figures 2F, 2G, 3F, 3G) at concentrations within therapeutic plasma ranges

claim: Diflunisal suppressed the growth of p300-dependent leukemia cell lines expressing AML1-ETO fusion protein in vitro and in vivo.
source: Finally, we found that diflunisal suppressed the growth of p300-dependent leukemia cell lines expressing AML1-ETO fusion protein in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: Supported by cell viability assays (Figure 4B), apoptosis assays (Figure 4C, D), and xenograft tumor growth data (Figure 5A-D)

claim: Salicylate does not inhibit GCN5 or PCAF acetyltransferases at concentrations that inhibit p300 and CBP.
source: Figure 1A shows recombinant p300, CBP, GCN5, or PCAF and histones were incubated with 14C-labeled acetyl-CoA with or without sodium salicylate
evidence: Figure 1A demonstrates selective inhibition of p300 and CBP but not GCN5 or PCAF by salicylate

claim: The thermal unfolding temperature of p300/acetyl-CoA is 48.6°C.
source: This experiment revealed that the thermal unfolding temperature of p300/acetyl-CoA was 48.6°C
evidence: Measured by thermal stability assay with SYPRO orange dye (Figure 1B)

claim: Treatment with 10 mM salicylate reduced the p300 unfolding temperature to 46.1°C.
source: while treatment with 10 and 25 mM salicylate reduced the unfolding temperature to 46.1°C and 40.8°C, respectively
evidence: Measured by thermal stability assay (Figure 1B)

claim: Treatment with 25 mM salicylate reduced the p300 unfolding temperature to 40.8°C.
source: while treatment with 10 and 25 mM salicylate reduced the unfolding temperature to 46.1°C and 40.8°C, respectively
evidence: Measured by thermal stability assay (Figure 1B)

claim: Salicylate exhibits noncompetitive inhibition against histones.
source: Kinetic analysis of p300 acetyltransferase activity with various concentrations of acetyl-CoA (Figure 1C) and histone (Figure 1D) substrates revealed that salicylate exhibits direct competitive p300 inhibition against acetyl-CoA and noncompetitive inhibition against histones.
evidence: Demonstrated by Lineweaver-Burk kinetic analysis (Figure 1D)

claim: Addition of salicylate correlated with the deacetylation of H2A K5, K9, H2B K12/K15, and H3K56 in HEK293T cells.
source: Western blot analysis with antibodies against various specific acetyl-lysine modifications of histone H2A, H2B, H3, and H4 showed that addition of salicylate correlated with the deacetylation of H2A K5, K9, H2B K12/K15, and H3K56
evidence: Demonstrated by Western blot analysis with specific antibodies (Figure 2A)

claim: Overexpression of wild type p300 suppressed the effect of salicylate on H2BK12/K15 acetylation in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Overexpression of WT p300 suppressed the effect of salicylate in a dose-dependent manner and increased H2BK12/K15 acetylation (Figure 2B)
evidence: Demonstrated by Western blot analysis of cells transfected with increasing amounts of p300 (Figure 2B)

claim: Overexpression of catalytically inactive p300 mutants did not suppress the effect of salicylate on H2BK12/K15 acetylation.
source: but overexpression of catalytically inactive p300 mutants (Figure 2C) and PCAF did not
evidence: Demonstrated by Western blot analysis of cells transfected with p300 Y1503A and F1504A mutants (Figure 2C)

claim: Overexpression of PCAF did not suppress the effect of salicylate on H2BK12/K15 acetylation.
source: but overexpression of catalytically inactive p300 mutants (Figure 2C) and PCAF did not (Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2)
evidence: Demonstrated by Western blot analysis of cells transfected with PCAF (Figure 2D)

claim: The IC50 of salicylate strongly correlated with the amount of transfected p300 but not PCAF.
source: Furthermore, the IC50 of salicylate strongly correlated with the amount of transfected p300 but not PCAF (Figure 2E).
evidence: Demonstrated by plotting IC50 values against plasmid amounts (Figure 2E)

claim: Salicylate decreased acetylation of NF-κB in a dose-dependent manner.

claim: Salicylate decreased acetylation of p53 in a dose-dependent manner.

claim: Salicylate activates AMPK as measured by phosphorylation of acetyl-CoA carboxylase (ACC).
source: The levels of a phosphorylated form of acetyl-CoA carboxylase (ACC), an established AMPK target, increased in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2G).
evidence: Demonstrated by Western blot showing increased p-ACC levels (Figure 2G)

claim: Compound C suppressed p-ACC accumulation in response to salicylate.

evidence: Demonstrated by Western blot analysis (Figure 2G)

claim: Compound C did not inhibit deacetylation of acetylated H2BK12/K15 or acetyl-p53K382 induced by salicylate.

claim: Salicylate-mediated protein deacetylation is not dependent on AMPK activation and activity.

claim: Anacardic acid contains a salicylic acid moiety linked to a long alkyl chain.
